metadata.document_title: RHOBS Synthetic Monitoring - Interactive Learning Guide
metadata.purpose: Hands-on learning path for understanding RHOBS synthetic monitoring through practical testing
learning_objectives: Understand RHOBS architecture and data flows
Gain hands-on experience with monitoring tools

learning_path.description: Recommended sequence for new developers to learn the system

rosa_hcp.title: ROSA HCP (Hosted Control Plane)
rosa_hcp.description: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS with hosted control plane. Control plane runs on a management cluster, worker nodes in customer AWS account.
rosa_hcp.why_it_matters: Understanding HCP architecture is critical for debugging observability flows.

remote_write.title: Prometheus Remote Write
remote_write.description: Protocol for forwarding metrics from Prometheus to remote storage (RHOBS/Thanos).
remote_write.why_it_matters: Metrics won't appear in RHOBS without properly configured remote write.

synthetic_monitoring.title: Synthetic Monitoring
synthetic_monitoring.description: External probing of services to validate availability independent of internal monitoring.
synthetic_monitoring.why_it_matters: Provides early detection of customer-facing outages.

objectives: Learn ROSA HCP cluster creation workflow
Learn how to monitor cluster provisioning

common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always verify TEST_SECTOR is set before creation

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Not waiting for cluster to be fully ready
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Use 'rosa logs install -f' to watch until completion

test_execution.objective: Create a ROSA HCP cluster that serves as the foundation for learning observability data flows

steps.title: Generate Unique Cluster Name
steps.learning_note: Using timestamps ensures unique names and helps track when clusters were created for cleanup
steps.command:
export TEST_CLUSTER_NAME="metrics-test-$(date +%s)"
echo "Creating cluster: $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME"
steps.expected_output: Creating cluster: metrics-test-1739901234
steps.why_this_step: Prevents naming conflicts and makes cluster identification easier

steps.title: Create ROSA HCP Cluster
steps.learning_note: The --hosted-cp flag creates a Hosted Control Plane cluster. Notice how the control plane components won't run in your AWS account.
steps.command:
rosa create cluster \
  --cluster-name=$TEST_CLUSTER_NAME \
  --sts \
  --mode=auto \
  --hosted-cp \
  --properties=provision-shard-id:srep-dev \
  --region=$TEST_REGION \
  --yes
steps.expected_output:
I: Creating cluster 'metrics-test-XXXXXXX'
I: To view a list of clusters and their status, run 'rosa list clusters'
steps.why_this_step: Initiates cluster creation. The provision-shard-id:srep-dev ensures the cluster is created in the test environment.

common_errors.solution: Run 'ocm list clusters --parameter search="sector is srep-dev"' and delete old test clusters
common_errors.learn_more: Sectors have quota limits to prevent resource exhaustion

steps.title: Monitor Cluster Installation
steps.learning_note: Watch the installation logs to understand the provisioning process. Notice the different phases: DNS, control plane, workers.
steps.command: rosa logs install --cluster $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME -f
steps.expected_output: Shows real-time installation progress ending with 'cluster is ready'
steps.why_this_step: Learn what happens during cluster provisioning and how to diagnose installation failures

common_errors.error: Installation stuck at 'Waiting for control plane'
common_errors.solution: Usually resolves in 10-15 min. If stuck >30 min, check AWS service status
common_errors.learn_more: Control plane provisioning involves creating load balancers, security groups in AWS

steps.title: Capture Cluster Metadata
steps.learning_note: The cluster ID is used throughout RHOBS for labeling metrics and logs. The API URL is what synthetic monitoring will probe.
steps.expected_output:
Cluster ID: abc123xyz
API URL: https://api.abc123xyz.p1.openshiftapps.com:6443
steps.why_this_step: These values are essential for querying observability data in later tests

success_criteria: CLUSTER_ID variable is set and non-empty
CLUSTER_API_URL is accessible (returns 403 without auth is OK)
validation.how_to_verify: Run: rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME | grep State
validation.what_success_means: You've successfully provisioned infrastructure that will generate observability data
validation.what_failure_means: Cannot proceed with learning observability flows without a working cluster

common_failures.cause: Typo in sector name or sector doesn't exist
common_failures.prevention: Always verify environment variables before cluster creation

next_steps.on_success: Proceed to Test 2 (Logs Flow) to learn how application and audit logs flow to Loki
bonus_exploration: Login to the cluster: rosa create admin -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
Explore the HostedCluster CR on the management cluster
Check cluster monitoring stack: oc get pods -n openshift-monitoring

metadata.name: test_2_logs_flow
metadata.title: Trace Logs from Application to Loki

objectives: Master log label usage for filtering

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Querying Loki immediately after deploying workload
common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: No results, incorrectly assume log forwarding is broken
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Wait 5-10 minutes for logs to propagate. Check local logs first with 'oc logs'

common_beginner_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting to escape special characters in LogQL
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Use double quotes around literal strings, escape $ signs

test_execution.objective: Deploy a log-generating workload and trace its logs through the forwarding pipeline to Loki, learning how to query and filter logs

steps.title: Create a Unique Log Marker
steps.learning_note: This marker makes your logs easily searchable in Loki. In production, you'd use structured logging with consistent fields.
steps.command:
export LOG_MARKER="e2e-test-$(date +%s)-$(uuidgen | cut -d- -f1)"
echo "Log marker: $LOG_MARKER"
steps.expected_output: Log marker: e2e-test-1739901234-a1b2c3d4
steps.why_this_step: Demonstrates how to make logs searchable and traceable

steps.title: Deploy Log-Generating Pod
steps.learning_note: This simple pod generates INFO, WARN, and ERROR logs. Notice how container logs go to stdout - this is the standard pattern for containerized apps.
steps.command:
cat <<EOF | oc apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: log-generator
  namespace: default
  labels:
    app: log-generator
spec:
  containers:
  - name: logger
    image: busybox:latest
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
    args:
      - |
        while true; do
          echo "INFO: $LOG_MARKER - Test log entry \$(date)"
          echo "WARN: $LOG_MARKER - Warning message \$(date)"
          echo "ERROR: $LOG_MARKER - Error message \$(date)"
          sleep 10
        done
EOF
steps.expected_output: pod/log-generator created
steps.why_this_step: Learn the standard pattern for containerized application logging

steps.title: Verify Local Logs
steps.learning_note: Always verify logs locally before checking remote systems. This confirms the application is actually generating logs.
steps.command:
oc wait --for=condition=Ready pod/log-generator -n default --timeout=60s
oc logs -n default log-generator --tail=10
steps.expected_output: Shows recent log lines with your LOG_MARKER
steps.why_this_step: Teaches the debugging principle: verify data at the source before checking downstream systems

steps.title: Wait for Log Propagation
steps.learning_note: Logs flow: Container stdout → Node log file → fluentd/vector → Loki. This typically takes 2-5 minutes.
steps.command:
echo "Waiting 5 minutes for logs to reach Loki..."
echo "While waiting, read about the log pipeline in the concepts section"
sleep 300
steps.expected_output: 5 minute countdown
steps.why_this_step: Learn realistic expectations for observability data latency

steps.title: Query Application Logs from Loki
steps.learning_note: LogQL syntax: {label_filters} |= "text search". Labels are indexed, text searches are not. Use labels for filtering when possible.
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode 'query={cluster_id="'$CLUSTER_ID'",namespace="default"} |= "'$LOG_MARKER'"' \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query_range" | jq -r '.data.result[0].values[][1]'
steps.expected_output: Shows your log lines from Loki
steps.why_this_step: Learn LogQL basics and how to verify logs reached Loki

common_errors.solution: 1. Check local logs still generating 2. Verify LOKI_TOKEN is valid 3. Wait longer (up to 10 min) 4. Check log forwarding: oc get clusterlogging -A
common_errors.learn_more: Log forwarding requires ClusterLogging and ClusterLogForwarder CRs

steps.title: Explore Log Labels
steps.learning_note: Labels are how you filter logs in Loki. Key labels: cluster_id, namespace, pod, container. These are automatically added by the log forwarder.
steps.command:
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOKI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode 'query={cluster_id="'$CLUSTER_ID'"} |= "'$LOG_MARKER'"' \
  --data-urlencode "limit=1" \
  "$LOKI_API_URL/loki/api/v1/query_range" | jq '.data.result[0].stream'
steps.expected_output: Shows all labels on your log stream
steps.why_this_step: Understanding labels is critical for efficient log queries

steps.title: Query Logs in Grafana
steps.learning_note: Grafana Explore provides a UI for building LogQL queries. Use it to learn query syntax, then use API for automation.
steps.command:
echo "Open Grafana at: $GRAFANA_URL"
echo "Navigate to: Explore → Select Loki datasource"
echo "Query: {cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\",namespace=\"default\"} |= \"$LOG_MARKER\""
echo ""
echo "Try these filters:"
echo "- Filter by ERROR: {cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"} |= \"$LOG_MARKER\" |= \"ERROR\""
echo "- Count logs: count_over_time({cluster_id=\"$CLUSTER_ID\"} |= \"$LOG_MARKER\" [5m])"
steps.expected_output: Instructions for Grafana exploration
steps.why_this_step: Learn the tool SREs use daily for log analysis

success_criteria: Log labels include cluster_id, namespace, pod, container
validation.how_to_verify: Run step 5 query and verify results
validation.what_success_means: You understand the complete log pipeline and can query logs for troubleshooting
validation.what_failure_means: Log forwarding may be misconfigured, preventing you from debugging cluster issues

common_failures.symptom: No logs in Loki after 10 minutes
common_failures.cause: Log forwarding not configured or broken
debug_steps: Check ClusterLogging exists: oc get clusterlogging -A
Check logging operator: oc get pods -n openshift-logging
Check forwarder config: oc get clusterlogforwarder -A -o yaml
common_failures.fix: For HCP clusters, log forwarding should be automatic. Contact team if missing.
common_failures.prevention: Always verify log forwarding is configured before relying on Loki

next_steps.on_success: Proceed to Test 3 (Synthetic Monitoring) to learn how external probes validate cluster availability

metadata.name: test_3_synthetic_monitoring
metadata.title: Watch Synthetic Monitoring Detect Your Cluster

objectives: Understand the complete synthetic monitoring architecture
Practice reading component logs to trace data flows

common_beginner_mistakes.consequence: Think RMO is broken, when it's just slow
common_beginner_mistakes.how_to_avoid: RMO polls HostedClusters every 60s. Wait at least 2-3 minutes after cluster creation.
probe_success=0 means cluster API is unreachable, not that monitoring is broken

test_execution.objective: Follow your cluster through the complete synthetic monitoring lifecycle: detection → registration → execution → metrics → cleanup

steps.title: Login to Management Cluster
steps.learning_note: The Management Cluster hosts the control planes for HCP clusters. route-monitor-operator runs here and watches HostedCluster CRs.
steps.command:
# Get MC for srep-dev sector
export MC_CLUSTER_ID=$(ocm get /api/osd_fleet_mgmt/v1/management_clusters | jq -r '.items[] | select(.sector == "srep-dev") | .cluster_management_reference.cluster_id' | head -1)

echo "Management Cluster: $MC_CLUSTER_ID"
ocm backplane login $MC_CLUSTER_ID
oc whoami
steps.expected_output: Successfully logged in to MC
steps.why_this_step: Learn the HCP architecture: tenant clusters have CRs on MCs

steps.title: Find route-monitor-operator
steps.learning_note: RMO is the component that discovers new clusters and registers probes. Understanding where it runs is key to debugging.
steps.expected_output: Shows RMO deployment with READY status
steps.why_this_step: Learn how to locate operators in a multi-tenant cluster

steps.title: Verify RMO Configuration
steps.learning_note: RMO needs to know the RHOBS API URL to register probes. This is configured via environment variable.
steps.command: oc get deployment -n $RMO_NS route-monitor-operator -o yaml | grep -A3 'probe-api-url'
steps.expected_output: Shows probe-api-url pointing to RHOBS synthetics API
steps.why_this_step: Learn how operators are configured and how to verify configuration

common_errors.solution: RMO not configured for this MC. Check app-interface configuration.
common_errors.learn_more: Configuration is managed via app-interface GitOps

steps.title: Find Your Cluster's HostedCluster CR
steps.learning_note: HostedCluster CRs represent tenant clusters on the MC. RMO watches these CRs to discover new clusters.
steps.expected_output: Shows HostedCluster CR with API endpoint in status
steps.why_this_step: Learn how HCP architecture represents tenant clusters

steps.title: Watch RMO Logs for Discovery
steps.learning_note: RMO polls for HostedClusters periodically. Watch the logs to see it discover your cluster.
steps.command:
echo "Watching RMO logs for your cluster..."
oc logs -n $RMO_NS deployment/route-monitor-operator --tail=20 | grep -i "$TEST_CLUSTER_NAME\|hostedcluster"
echo ""
echo "If nothing appears, RMO may not have polled yet. Check recent logs:"
oc logs -n $RMO_NS deployment/route-monitor-operator --tail=50
steps.expected_output: Logs showing HostedCluster detection
steps.why_this_step: Learn to read operator logs to understand what the operator is doing

steps.title: Query RHOBS API for Registered Probe
steps.learning_note: After discovering your cluster, RMO calls the RHOBS API to register a probe. The probe config is stored as a ConfigMap.
steps.command:
echo "Waiting 2 minutes for RMO to register probe..."
sleep 120

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes" | \
  jq -r '.probes[] | select(.labels.cluster_id == "'$CLUSTER_ID'")' | head -30

export PROBE_ID=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/probes" | \
  jq -r '.probes[] | select(.labels.cluster_id == "'$CLUSTER_ID'") | .id')

echo ""
echo "Probe ID: $PROBE_ID"
steps.expected_output: Shows probe object with your cluster_id
steps.why_this_step: Learn how probe configuration is stored and accessed

common_errors.solution: Wait longer (up to 5 min) or check RMO logs for errors
common_errors.learn_more: RMO may retry on API errors

steps.title: Login to RHOBS Cell and Find Agent
steps.learning_note: The rhobs-synthetics-agent runs on RHOBS cell clusters. It polls the API for probes and creates Probe CRs for blackbox-exporter.
steps.command:
# Get RHOBS cell cluster ID from team or app-interface
echo "Ask team for RHOBS cell cluster ID for your region: $TEST_REGION"
echo "Or check app-interface for synthetics-agent deployment"
echo ""
echo "export RHOBS_CLUSTER_ID=<rhobs-cell-cluster-id>"
echo "ocm backplane login \$RHOBS_CLUSTER_ID"
steps.expected_output: Instructions to login to RHOBS cell
steps.why_this_step: Learn the distributed architecture of synthetic monitoring

steps.title: Watch Agent Create Probe CR
steps.learning_note: The agent polls the API every 30-60s. When it finds your probe, it creates a Probe CR that blackbox-exporter consumes.
steps.command:
export AGENT_NS=$(oc get deployment -A | grep synthetics-agent | awk '{print $1}')
echo "Agent namespace: $AGENT_NS"

echo "Watching agent logs..."
oc logs -n $AGENT_NS deployment/rhobs-synthetics-agent --tail=20 | grep -i probe

echo ""
echo "Waiting 60s for agent to poll and create Probe CR..."
sleep 60

oc get probes -n $AGENT_NS | grep $CLUSTER_ID
steps.expected_output: Shows Probe CR for your cluster
steps.why_this_step: Learn how configuration flows from API to execution

steps.title: Verify Blackbox Exporter Execution
steps.learning_note: Blackbox exporter reads Probe CRs and executes HTTP probes. It exposes probe_success, probe_duration_seconds metrics.
steps.command:
oc logs -n $AGENT_NS deployment/synthetics-blackbox-prober --tail=50 | grep -i "$CLUSTER_API_URL\|probe"

echo ""
echo "Querying Prometheus for probe metrics..."
oc exec -n $AGENT_NS prometheus-rhobs-synthetics-0 -- \
  promtool query instant http://localhost:9090 \
  'probe_success{cluster_id="'$CLUSTER_ID'"}'
steps.expected_output: Shows probe_success metric with value 1 or 0
steps.why_this_step: Learn how to verify probe execution and interpret results

steps.title: Query Probe Metrics in RHOBS
steps.learning_note: Metrics are remote-written from RHOBS cell Prometheus to Thanos. This typically takes 2-5 minutes.
steps.command:
echo "Waiting 5 minutes for metrics to reach RHOBS/Thanos..."
sleep 300

curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $RHOBS_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode 'query=probe_success{cluster_id="'$CLUSTER_ID'"}' \
  "$RHOBS_API_URL/api/metrics/v1/$RHOBS_TENANT/api/v1/query" | \
  jq '.data.result[]'
steps.expected_output: Shows probe_success metric with labels and value
steps.why_this_step: Complete the learning journey: data flows from probe → Prometheus → Thanos → RHOBS API

success_criteria: Probe CR created on RHOBS cell
validation.how_to_verify: Run step 10 and verify probe_success metric exists
validation.what_success_means: You can now debug the entire synthetic monitoring stack and understand how clusters are automatically monitored
validation.what_failure_means: Gaps in understanding the distributed monitoring architecture

common_failures.cause: Cluster API not reachable from RHOBS cell
debug_steps: Test from RHOBS cell: oc debug node/<node> -- curl -v https://<api-url>:6443/readyz
Check cluster API is healthy: rosa describe cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME
Check blackbox logs for detailed error
common_failures.fix: Usually network/firewall issue. Check VPC peering and security groups.
common_failures.prevention: Verify network connectivity before deploying monitoring

next_steps.on_success: Congratulations! You've completed the RHOBS learning path. You now understand metrics, logs, and synthetic monitoring.
bonus_exploration: Delete the cluster and watch probe cleanup: rosa delete cluster -c $TEST_CLUSTER_NAME --yes
Read the RMO code to understand the reconciliation logic
